---
title: "Citing vidigi"
---

<!-- Keep this page in sync with the "Citation" section of README.md. -->

If you use vidigi in your work, please cite the paper:

> Rosser, S., & Chalk, D. (2026). Vidigi: A Python library for interactive-animated visualisations of discrete event simulation models. *Journal of Simulation*. Advance online publication. <https://doi.org/10.1080/17477778.2026.2663849>

## BibTeX

```bibtex
@article{rosser2026vidigi,
  title     = {Vidigi: a Python library for interactive-animated visualisations of discrete event simulation models},
  author    = {Rosser, Sammi and Chalk, Daniel},
  journal   = {Journal of Simulation},
  year      = {2026},
  publisher = {Taylor \& Francis},
  doi       = {10.1080/17477778.2026.2663849}
}
```

## Citing a specific version

To cite a specific release of the software, use its Zenodo archive. The [all-versions DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14635602) always resolves to the latest release; each release also has its own version-specific DOI on the [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14635602).

GitHub's **Cite this repository** button generates both the paper and software citations from the [`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/hsma-tools/vidigi/blob/main/CITATION.cff) file in the repository root.
